haors.name: Choto Hijla- Baro Hijlar Beel Haor

haor_src: Department of Bangladesh Haor and Wetlands Development, Classification of Wetlands of Bangladesh, Vol. 3, Annexure 2: Haors of Bangladesh (2016), after the Master Plan of Haor Area (BHWDB 2012). Area by upazila; a haor that spans upazilas is summed.
haor_place: Each haor is drawn as a circle of its own area, placed on wet ground (ESA WorldCover 2021) inside the upazila or upazilas it lies in. The position is approximate; Tanguar and Hakaluki use their mapped outlines.

beels.name: Chalan Beel
beels.where: Sirajganj, Pabna and Natore (Raiganj, Chatmohar, Tarash, Singra)
beels.note: The largest beel in the country. The Atrai is its main feeder; the Baral and Gumani drain it towards the Jamuna.

beels.name: Arial Beel
beels.where: Dhaka and Munshiganj, between the Padma and the Dhaleshwari
beels.note: Heavy clay. It floods deep each monsoon from rain that cannot drain while the rivers are high, and much of it stays wet through the dry season.

beels.name: Beel Dakatia
facts: usually under 0.5 to 2 m of water
beels.note: Waterlogged since the polder cut it off from the tides: the channels silted up while the land inside sank.

beels.name: Baikka Beel
beels.note: A permanent sanctuary inside Hail Haor, protected since 2003; one of the best places to count wintering ducks.

beel_src: Banglapedia: Chalan Beel, Arial Beel, Beel Dakatia, Beel, Haors and Wetlands.
wet_src: ESA WorldCover 2021, permanent water and herbaceous wetland, 270 m (dry season: the monsoon spread is far larger).

sites.name: Tanguar Haor
sites.species: 69 waterbird species in the 2008 to 2021 censuses, 41 of them migrants; 23 of the 41 migrants declined, Baer's pochard among them.
sites.src: 2010 and 2013: lowest and highest of the IUCN Bangladesh censuses, Alam et al. 2023, Avian Conservation and Ecology 18(1):18. 2015 to 2019: IUCN, Bangladesh Bird Club and Forest Department January counts (The Daily Star, 25 Jan 2019; 2019 rounded). 2022 and 2024: Bangladesh Bird Club with IUCN (bdnews24, 27 Mar 2026; 2022 rounded).

sites.name: Hakaluki Haor
sites.src: Bangladesh Bird Club; 2023 with IUCN Bangladesh (The Daily Star). No census in 2021 or 2022.

sites.name: Baikka Beel, Hail Haor
sites.src: Bangladesh Bird Club annual census (The Daily Star, 2025).

sites.name: Eastern Sundarbans
sites.species: Ruddy shelduck, masked finfoot (critically endangered), lesser sand plover.
sites.src: Regional Flyway Initiative site selection, Bangladesh, 2024 (ranked first).

sites.name: Eastern Meghna delta
sites.species: Indian skimmer (endangered), spoon-billed sandpiper (critically endangered), lesser sand plover, broad-billed sandpiper.

sites.name: Hatiya and Nijhum Dwip
sites.species: Indian skimmer, lesser sand plover, black-headed ibis.

sites.name: Central Meghna delta
sites.species: Black-headed ibis, lesser sand plover, common shelduck.

sites.name: Sonadia Island
sites.species: Lesser sand plover and the critically endangered spoon-billed sandpiper.

birds.national: Tanguar Haor held about 43% of the 1.2 million waterbirds counted in Bangladesh from 2008 to 2015 (Thompson et al. 2018, cited by Alam et al. 2023).
birds.season: Most arrive in November and leave by March. Bangladesh sits on the Central Asian and the East Asian-Australasian flyways.
